name: a-new-launch-forgets-expected-exits-of-the-old-one
description: PowerUp stops its own session by switching to remote mode, then switches back and sends a message, which relaunches the session resuming the stored id. That resume fails at once: the failure is still retried as a fresh session, even though the stop PowerUp caused never reported an exit.
reason: PowerUp counts the exits it causes so they are not taken for crashes. A relaunch retires the old process, whose exit then never arrives, so a count left over from it would swallow the next real exit and turn off the resume retry.
source: AppState.startSession (comment: 'Any still-pending expected termination can therefore never arrive — clear the counter'); AppState.handleTermination

script.reason: App launch resumes the stored conversation.
Remote mode stops PowerUp's own session; PowerUp expects its exit.
Back to built-in mode. Nothing starts until the next message.
The message relaunches the session, resuming the stored id again.
The resume fails before any init. This is the new launch's exit, not the one PowerUp expected.

transcript.text: Remote control mode — buttons and voice now drive your existing Claude session.
Built-in session mode — PowerUp runs its own Claude session again.
Couldn't resume the previous session — starting a fresh one.
